source.anchor: S4.Thmtheorem4 literal tau; S4.3 unnamed tau envelope and tau/beta smallness; private shifted target probability before orthogonal transport.
source.original_text: The concrete threshold eventually lies below one quarter of the actual target Gaussian bias. 0\le\tau_{d,q}\le\min\!\left\{\frac12,\frac\beta4\right\}. Fix a positive real numerical scale \(C\), then \(0<\delta<1\). There is one natural cutoff \(d_0(C,\delta)\), chosen before all varying \(d,\kappa,q\). The cutoff is not asserted uniform over unbounded \(C\). For every natural \(d\ge d_0(C,\delta)\), real \(2\le\kappa\le d^{1-\delta}\), and natural \(q\ge0\) with \(q\le(\delta/256)\sqrt\kappa\log d\), put \(n=2q+1\). The exact integer query-cap regime includes \(q=0\); it is not an expected-cost statement. Use \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\), \(U\sim N(0,\Lambda^{-1})\), and \(Q(x)=\sum_i\cos(n\theta_i)x_i^2\). Set \(M=\mathbb E\|U\|^2\), \(b=\mathbb E Q(U)\), and \(\beta=|b|/M\). Lean uses the same grid with zero-based finite coordinates. The threshold is literal: \(\tau_{d,q}=C[(q+1)\sqrt{\log d/d}+(q+1)(q+1+\log d)\log d/d]\). All dimension, frequency, inverse-covariance, integrability, positivity and uniform-smallness conditions are established internally. This is a numerical auxiliary family for each fixed positive \(C\). The separate concentration argument must still produce one sufficiently large absolute \(C\), fixed before \(\delta\); specializing the family to that value then yields a \(\delta\)-only cutoff. No \(C\)-premise is added to either main lower bound.

lean_statement.statement:
∀ (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) {δ : ℝ} (hδ0 : 0 < δ) (hδ1 : δ < 1),
  ∃ d₀ : ℕ, ∀ (d : ℕ), d₀ ≤ d → ∀ (κ : ℝ), 2 ≤ κ →
    κ ≤ (d : ℝ) ^ (1 - δ) → ∀ (q : ℕ),
    (q : ℝ) ≤ (δ / 256) * Real.sqrt κ * Real.log (d : ℝ) →
    let n : ℕ := 2 * q + 1
    let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
    let eigenvalue : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)
    let Λ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := Matrix.diagonal eigenvalue
    let μ : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
      multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) Λ⁻¹
    let Q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
      ∑ i : Fin d, Real.cos ((n : ℝ) * θ i) * (WithLp.ofLp x i) ^ 2
    let τ : ℝ := C * (((q : ℝ) + 1) * Real.sqrt (Real.log (d : ℝ) / (d : ℝ)) +
      (((q : ℝ) + 1) * ((q : ℝ) + 1 + Real.log (d : ℝ)) * Real.log (d : ℝ)) / (d : ℝ))
    let M : ℝ := ∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), ‖x‖ ^ 2 ∂μ
    let b : ℝ := ∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), Q x ∂μ
    let β : ℝ := |b| / M
    0 ≤ τ ∧ τ ≤ 1 / 2 ∧ τ ≤ β / 4

approved_definition_context: Natural numbers include zero. Universal/existential quantifiers and arrows have their usual dependent meanings; an existential threshold is an output witness. Real casts are the usual inclusions.

EuclideanSpace Real(Fin d) is d-dimensional Euclidean space; WithLp.ofLp exposes its coordinates. Matrix.diagonal has the displayed diagonal and zero off-diagonal entries. Matrix inverse is standard total inverse, agreeing with ordinary inverse on invertible matrices.

multivariateGaussian m S is the standard Mathlib Gaussian measure obtained from standard Gaussian by the affine map with matrix square root CFC.sqrt S. For positive semidefinite S its covariance is S; the standard non-PSD convention degenerates to Dirac at m. No project-owned fallback definition is added.

Integrals are real Bochner integrals under the displayed measure with standard totalized conventions. The Euclidean norm is the full norm, not divided by dimension. Absolute value and natural powers have their usual meanings.
Real.log, Real.sqrt and real powers are standard real functions. For positive x, x^r=exp(log(x)*r); square root is nonnegative. Every constant is its literal rational value.

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every real number C and every hypothesis hC that 0 < C, and then for every real number δ and hypotheses hδ0 that 0 < δ and hδ1 that δ < 1, there exists a natural number d₀ with the following property. For every natural number d, if d₀ ≤ d, then for every real number κ, if 2 ≤ κ and κ ≤ (d : ℝ)^(1 − δ), then for every natural number q, if
(q : ℝ) ≤ (δ / 256) · sqrt(κ) · log(d : ℝ),
the definitions and conclusion below apply. Natural numbers include zero. Thus the existential dimension threshold is chosen after C and δ and before d, κ, and q; it is an output witness, not an input hypothesis.

Set n := 2q + 1, a natural number. Index coordinates by Fin d, equivalently by integers i = 0, …, d − 1. For such an index let
θᵢ := ((i : ℝ) + 1/2) · π / (d : ℝ),
λᵢ := (κ + 1)/2 + ((κ − 1)/2) · cos(θᵢ),
and let Λ be the real d-by-d diagonal matrix with diagonal entries λᵢ and zero entries off the diagonal. Let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), the full d-dimensional Euclidean space, and let
μ := multivariateGaussian(0 ∈ E, Λ⁻¹).
Here Λ⁻¹ is the standard total matrix inverse, agreeing with the ordinary inverse on invertible matrices. The Gaussian constructor is the standard measure obtained by pushing forward the standard Gaussian by the affine map with mean 0 and matrix square root CFC.sqrt(Λ⁻¹). For a positive semidefinite covariance argument its covariance is that argument; its stipulated non-positive-semidefinite convention gives the point mass at the mean. This is the supplied Gaussian definition.

For x ∈ E, write xᵢ := WithLp.ofLp(x)(i) for its real coordinate and define the real quadratic function
Q(x) := ∑_{i ∈ Fin d} cos((n : ℝ) · θᵢ) · xᵢ².
Define the real numbers
τ := C · (((q : ℝ) + 1) · sqrt(log(d : ℝ)/(d : ℝ))
          + ((((q : ℝ) + 1) · ((q : ℝ) + 1 + log(d : ℝ)) · log(d : ℝ))/(d : ℝ))),
M := ∫_{x ∈ E} ‖x‖² dμ(x),
b := ∫_{x ∈ E} Q(x) dμ(x),
and β := |b|/M.
Both integrals are real Bochner integrals with respect to this displayed Gaussian measure μ, with their standard totalized conventions. The norm in M is the full Euclidean norm; there is no division of ‖x‖² by d. The scalar b is the signed integral of Q, and only afterwards is absolute value taken in β. All real divisions, logarithms, square roots, real powers, and matrix inverses carry the supplied standard meanings and totalized conventions. For positive t, t^r means exp(log(t) · r), and square root is nonnegative. Every displayed numerical constant, including 1/2 and 256, has its literal rational value.

The conclusion is the conjunction
0 ≤ τ,   τ ≤ 1/2,   and   τ ≤ β/4.
All three inequalities hold for every d, κ, and q in the stated order and under the stated hypotheses, using the same d₀ for the fixed C and δ. The upper bound on q is an input restriction. The upper bounds on τ, including τ ≤ 1/2 and τ ≤ β/4, are conclusions about the defined output quantity τ. The endpoints in 2 ≤ κ, κ ≤ d^(1 − δ), q ≤ (δ/256)sqrt(κ)log d, d₀ ≤ d, and all three concluding inequalities are inclusive; only 0 < C, 0 < δ, and δ < 1 are strict. No additional independent assumptions on d₀, n, μ, M, b, β, or τ are supplied.

private_standard_definition_context: ENNReal.toReal is the usual real conversion with zero at infinity; genuine finite-mass interpretation must be internally justified.

The private statement has the same literal inverse-precision Gaussian and coordinate cosine quadratic. Its threshold is the exact displayed two-term formula; positivity, moments, uniform signal mass and event probability are not inputs.
